chunks.content: ## Importing and Setting Up Files in CLO This section explains how to import pattern and model files into CLO 3D, organize them in the 2D and 3D windows, and prepare the workspace for jacket construction. Key terms include **library window**, **3D window**, **2D window**, **pattern files (.dxf)**, and **arrangement points**. - Open the library window, locate the model file named *femalev2* and the end-of-day file *Elton*. - Double-click the *fv2vv.mvt* file and drag it into the 3D window to load the avatar. - Open the *Proteus Files* folder in the library; find *bimbasic.jacket*. - Double-click or drag *jacket-femur.dxf* into the 2D or 3D window to import the jacket pattern pieces. - In the 2D window, press **Ctrl + A** to select all pattern pieces. - Use the menu to select **column-linked files**, match the files, and deny the line (to align pattern halves). - Copy and mirror one half of the pattern by pressing **Shift** and moving it to the opposite side. - Align the back panel and collar pieces near their original positions in the 2D window. - In the 3D toolbar, select **All 2D Arrangement Positions** to sync the 2D and 3D views. - Activate the arrangement points in the 3D vertical toolbar to display blue arrangement points around the 3D avatar. ## Positioning and Layering Pattern Pieces This section details how to position front, back, and sleeve panels with correct layering and alignment using CLO's positioning tools and view rotations. Important terms include **position tool**, **layer relationships**, and **3D panel assembly**. - Select all files in the 2D window; move pattern pieces to the corresponding arrangement points in the 3D window. - Use the position tool to layer the back panel behind the front panel. - Rotate the 3D view (left, right, front, back) to check spacing between panels and verify layer relationships. - In the 2D window, hold **Shift** and select left and right front panels to create a 3D panel. - In the 3D window, position the right front piece on top of the left front piece; do the same for right and left back pieces. - Confirm the correct gap and layering between front and back pieces. - Select front and hanging panels simultaneously in 2D with **Shift**, then arrange them around the model using arrangement points in 3D. - Repeat arrangement for the back panel and sleeves, assigning them to the neck and arm points respectively. ## Sewing and Seam Alignment This section covers using the **Seam Seaming tool** to sew garment pieces together, emphasizing consistent seam direction for realistic simulation. It includes sewing front and back panels, sleeves, and collars. - In the 3D window, use the **Seam Seaming tool** to sew front and back panels. - Ensure the seam direction is consistent for proper fabric simulation. - Sew sleeves together with attention to seam alignment. - Attach the collar to the neckline, maintaining seam direction.

chunks.title: [Cantonese Subtitled Dubbing] CLO Official Tutorial Video ~ Basics Part p05 5. Making a Jacket
chunks.content: ## Sewing and Seam Alignment This section covers using the **Seam Seaming tool** to sew garment pieces together, emphasizing consistent seam direction for realistic simulation. It includes sewing front and back panels, sleeves, and collars. - In the 3D window, use the **Seam Seaming tool** to sew front and back panels. - Ensure the seam direction is consistent for proper fabric simulation. - Sew sleeves together with attention to seam alignment. - Attach the collar to the neckline, maintaining seam direction. - After sewing, switch the face to the front piece and change the function type to **Turn** in the sound editor for a flatter simulation result. ## Adding and Editing Buttons This section explains how to create, position, and duplicate buttons on the jacket using CLO's button tools and parameter settings. - In the 3D toolbar, select the button tool and click on the button baseline on the front piece. - The button line appears in the 2D window; the button image shows in 3D. - Use the **Move Button Tool** to select and adjust button positions in 2D. - Copy buttons to the symmetrical side via the menu to ensure bilateral symmetry. - Select button and buttonhole in the 2D window; adjust parameters in the dialog box (e.g., set value to 2). - Use the move button tool to fine-tune button and buttonhole positions on screen. - Activate simulation to observe natural button placement and fabric curvature. ## Folding and Hardening Techniques for Realistic Fabric Simulation This section covers folding lines, folding arrangement tools, and hardening to simulate fabric folds and stiffness, focusing on collars and back panels. - Use the 2D toolbar's **Folding Arrangement Tool** to create folding lines on panels (e.g., collar, back). - In the 3D window, click on folding lines to display positioning balls; drag arrows to fold fabric accordingly. - Adjust folding angles up to 360 degrees in the audio editor for realistic folds. - Avoid overlapping folds with outer fabric layers during manipulation. - Right-click on versions in 3D to select **Hardening** mode, making panels temporarily editable and easier to fold. - Activate simulation to visualize folds; use **W** key to create set-points and pull them for even collar folds. - For back panels, fold only the right back panel initially; set folding angle to 0 in attribute editor for precision. - Remove links between left and right back panels if necessary to fold them independently. - Undo operations with **Ctrl + Z** where needed to correct errors. ## Material and Fabric Setup This section describes selecting fabric materials, applying double layers for thickness, and configuring fabric properties to enhance garment realism. - In the library window, open the *FemaleV2* model posture document. - Open the *Fabric* file and select *Cotton Garbage* fabric; drag it into the fabric object window. - Apply the fabric to the 3D clothing and activate simulation. - Use the editor tool in the 2D window to compare the collar fabric layers.

chunks.title: [Cantonese Subtitled Dubbing] CLO Official Tutorial Video ~ Basics Part p05 5. Making a Jacket
chunks.content: ## Material and Fabric Setup This section describes selecting fabric materials, applying double layers for thickness, and configuring fabric properties to enhance garment realism. - In the library window, open the *FemaleV2* model posture document. - Open the *Fabric* file and select *Cotton Garbage* fabric; drag it into the fabric object window. - Apply the fabric to the 3D clothing and activate simulation. - Use the editor tool in the 2D window to compare the collar fabric layers. - The collar requires two fabric layers for increased thickness. - In the material editor, drag the fabric material down to add thickness—this is visible in both 2D and 3D windows. - Enter the thickness value of the fabric in the material editor options. - Enable double-layer display in the material editor to preview thickness effects on the collar in 3D. - Use the **Improve Quality** tool in the 3D toolbar to enhance visual contrast and fabric detail. - Confirm changes by clicking OK, then apply and close simulation. ## Final Simulation and Adjustments This section outlines how to finalize garment simulation, adjust fold lines, and ensure natural fabric behavior before completion. - Use the simulation tool to activate garment physics and observe natural fabric behavior. - Rotate views to inspect garment from different angles (front, back, left, right). - Use frame tools to select baselines and reverse fold them into internal lines for realistic edges. - Adjust folding lines in the audio editor to refine folding angles and garment drape. - When satisfied with the folds and simulation, close the simulation mode. - Ensure all panels are properly linked or unlinked as required for accurate garment construction. - Perform any necessary undo commands to correct panel relationships or fold lines. - Confirm final garment appearance and simulation quality before exporting or proceeding to additional design steps.
